references.text: Joshua receives the same command to take off his sandals because the place where he stands is holy, a direct parallel to Moses' experience at the burning bush.
The Preacher urges caution when approaching God's house, reflecting the theme of reverence and holiness in God's presence.
Jacob acknowledges that the place where he is located is holy, God's house and the gate of heaven, similar to the recognition of holy ground.
Stephen quotes this event in his speech and confirms that God commanded Moses to take off his sandals because the place was holy.
The command to keep the Lord's sanctuary holy emphasizes the importance of honoring sacred places.
The people were forbidden from approaching Mount Sinai because it was holy, illustrating the same principle of boundaries around holy places.
